title: Lord What a Feeble Piece
description: Lord What a Feeble Piece in Tonic Solfa to ST. BRIDE, doh is Bb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 90, part 5, headed “The frailty and shortness of life”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Short Metre (6.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. BRIDE; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord what a fee-ble piece Is this our mor-tal frame! Our life how poor a tri-fle 'tis, That scarce de-serves the name!

lines: Our life how poor a trifle 'tis,
And every month, and every day
Just like a flood our hasty days
Well if our days must fly,
We'll keep their end in sight,
We'll spend them all in wisdom's way,
And let them speed their flight.
Soon we shall reach the peaceful shore

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. BRIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
